nodes.title: Why Segments ?
widgets_values:
In certain situations, placing an object entirely within a single tile is essential for achieving consistent results. By applying a mask to an object, it can be sampled separately from the rest of the image. The masked area will then be upscaled to match the tile size, enhancing its detail.

This technique can also be used to repair or modify elements by applying different settings, prompts, or denoise values using the function.

After the entire image is processed, the segmented areas will be handled. ImpactPack is compatible with TBG ETUR segmentation entries, making it possible to automate the selection process.

nodes.title: Why use Redux?
widgets_values:
Why use Redux?
Redux regenerates the image while preserving its overall composition and style.
A value of 1 means full reconstruction with strict adherence to the original
Lower values allow more creative freedom in the output
A value of 0 disables Redux entirely
If neither a Redux Clip nor a Style Model is connected, Redux will automatically be disabled
Redux is particularly useful for preserving fine materials, textures, and structural composition. In many cases, it can serve as a lightweight alternative to ControlNets.

nodes.title: VLM
widgets_values:
We have three ways to load VLMs:

1. **Standard** – Fully automatic setup. Supports all models except GGUF.

2. **GGUF** – Often requires a manual llama.cpp server installation, which can be complicated for some configurations. We provide prebuilt wheels, and installation is only required if you select the GGUF option.

3. **Fastest and Best Option: OpenAI-Compatible (Labs Server)** – Connect the Labs_upscaler node and enter the URL, port, and model name of your local or API-based Ollama or llama.cpp server with the Qwen GGUF model loaded.

4. Florence has now been fixed to run on Transformer versions 5 and above.

nodes.title: ControlNets
widgets_values:
You can add as many ControlNets as you like.
currently, the only available preprocessors are Depth, Canny, Canny Edge, and None. We’ve excluded Pose because the subject will be divided into tiles, making pose estimation ineffective in the cnet pipe you can add pose conventionaly to the croped conditioning in the refiner.

A global ControlNet strength modifier is available to help fine-tune all ControlNets at once.

The ControlNet preprocessor works directly on each tile, allowing it to operate at the tile's full resolution. This differs from other refiners like Ultimate Upscale, where the ControlNet input is cropped, and a tile only uses a small portion of the full ControlNet resolution. With our setup, each tile benefits from full-resolution preprocessing.

nodes.title: Reference Images (Flux2 / QwenEdit/Kontext )
widgets_values:
How to use the new reference-image ControlNet-style mode

This new mode lives in the `TBG ControlNet Pipe` node and works like a familiar ControlNet slider setup, but under the hood it is still a latent correction path, not a real ControlNet model.

1. Add a `TBG ControlNet Pipe` node to your workflow.

2. Set `reference_mode` to `Reference ControlNet` - it auto feeds the tile as ref.

3. Set the three new sliders:

   - `Strength` = how strongly the reference pulls the denoised latent

   - `Start %` = when the influence starts

   - `End %` = when the influence stops

4. Connect the `Controlnet_Pipe` output into your `TBG ETUR Refiner PRO` node’s `Controlnet_Pipe` input.

By setting the Preprocessor dropdown to None, the reference image will use the full-color tile. Selecting Depth uses a depth map as the reference image, while Canny uses a canny edge map. You can also combine and chain them together. If you connect an image to the slot in the ControlNet pipe, that image will be used as the reference image for all tiles.

Important note:
When strength is set to 1 (start = 0, end = 1), the node injects the reference image in the standard behavior. For all other values, the reference image is injected on a per-step basis, which behaves differently. If you want to use both modes simultaneously, you need to use two ControlNet Pipe nodes—one for each mode.
 have both use 2 controlnet pipe nodes 1 for each.

nodes.title: Only Upscale
widgets_values:
Set the Lab Node to Only Upscale to turn this into a fully functional Tiled Upscaler without prepairing things for the refiner.

We fine-tuned SeedVR2, Waifu, FlashVR, and others into a new multi-step Upscaler with adaptive sigmas.
Give them a try — they’re not the fastest option, but for consistent, high-quality upscaling, this is a solid solution.

For more details on what’s changed, please read the text field shown when creating the node and have a look into the Tooltips.
